handoff: Review #2: changes requested. Review #1's F1–F7 are fixed. Unit 1080/0, typecheck clean. 4 blocking: F1 norn init now installs hooks and skills for all four agents (B1, B13); F2 a bad notify.webhook makes doctor say 0 checks failed and skip the machine checks, with no FAIL config line (B48); F3 adapter config errors exit 1, not 6 'Config error' (B7); F4 migrate rewrites and reports files with no old key, just for yaml reformatting (B45). Minor: hookWindowMs tested directly, status hides config errors, doctor always checks claude, B54 file and host matching, duplication.

findings.title: norn init now installs hooks and skills for all four agents
findings.detail:
Since wiring builds every built-in agent (B13 fix), init loops over ports.agents and writes .codex/hooks.json, .opencode/plugins/norn.js, .gemini/settings.json and .gemini/skills in every repo, and its Next steps tell the person to commit them. Verified: `bun packages/cli/src/main.ts init` in a fresh repo with no config → .claude, .codex, .gemini, .opencode created. On main only Claude was set up. B1: 'setup is `norn init` and nothing else' for a solo Claude user; B13 asked that a built-in be usable, not installed everywhere. Doctor was narrowed to agents in use (agentsInUse); init and uninstall were not. Uninstall should still remove what any agent installed.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Use the same agents-in-use set (default agent, configured entries, agents named on workflow steps) for init's hook/skill install and Next steps; add an S1 test that a plain init writes only .claude.

findings.title: A bad notify.webhook does not give a FAIL config line; doctor says 0 checks failed
findings.detail:
Spec B48: 'a bad `notify.webhook` → `FAIL config: notify webhook: …` followed by the remaining doctor lines.' Verified with `notify: {webhook: not-a-url}` in the user file: doctor prints 'norn doctor: 0 checks failed ()', 'ok config .agents/norn.config.yaml', and skips every machine check ('machine checks skipped: they need a config that loads'). The value fails at schema load, so the build-time fallback never runs. The message also repeats the key: 'notify.webhook `notify.webhook` must be an http or https URL'. The B48 test (housekeeping.test.ts:462) covers only an ntfy URL that passes the schema and fails to build. Related: doctorPorts retries only with notifiers: [], so an agent or remote factory error throws again and crashes doctor; any non-CliFailure (a plain bug) is reported as config; ctx.ports(overrides) replaces the cached ports for later callers (context.ts:186-189).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: When config fails to load, report it as a FAIL config line (counted in the header, non-zero exit) and still run the checks that do not need it; dedupe the key in the message; add the B48 example itself as the test.

findings.title: Adapter config errors exit 1, not the config exit code
findings.detail:
adapterError throws failure(message, …, 'config_invalid'), and failure is 'Unexpected failure (exit 1)' (output.ts:56-57), so it gets the 'Error' title and exit 1. configError uses ExitCode.config (6) and the 'Config error' title for the same code. B7: 'every config error shown under the title "Config error" with its own exit code'. AGENTS.md: code branches on the exit code.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Build adapter errors with configError (or a CliFailure with ExitCode.config); test the exit code and title at S1 or S3.

findings.title: migrate rewrites and reports files that hold no old key
findings.detail:
The change test is doc.toString() !== raw. The yaml library normalises formatting, so a new-style file such as user `mode:    auto   # mine` is rewritten to `mode: auto # mine`, listed under changed, and printed as 'rewrote …', with nothing renamed or removed. A team file would also be staged. B45: migrate changes nothing when there is nothing to change. Found by the standards subagent with a bun script against migrateConfig.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Track whether the edit callback changed anything (a dirty flag) and write only then; add an S1 test with a new-style file in odd formatting → nothing changed, nothing staged.

findings.title: B28 still tested on the internal hookWindowMs
findings.detail:
decide.test.ts imports hookWindowMs from ../../src/policy.ts, and config-trace.test.ts:84 calls it too. implement#2 says B28 is tested at the S4 load seam; the internal-helper asserts remain.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Drop the direct hookWindowMs asserts, keeping the seam test.

findings.title: norn status hides a config error
findings.detail:
With `max_agents: 4` in the team file, `norn status` (with and without --json) prints an empty inbox and exits 0, because the view falls back to DEFAULT_CONFIG. It behaved the same on main, but B7 says 'any command that loads config'.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Surface the config error as an inbox or Unblock item, or as the config exit.

findings.title: doctor always checks claude
findings.detail:
config.agents always holds claude (BUILT_IN_AGENTS), so with `agent: codex` doctor still checks Claude.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Count an agents entry as in use only when a file sets it.

findings.title: B54 message and provider detection
findings.detail:
The B54 error blames `.agents/norn.config.yaml` (file: repo) even when no team file exists. providerFromUrl uses host.includes('github'), so a host like notgithub.example counts as GitHub. FileError.file is absolute for the user file and repo-relative for the others (store config.ts:121).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Match the host exactly (github.com / gitlab.com, or a subdomain).

findings.title: Duplication and leftovers
findings.detail:
Orphan JSDoc 'B48 (D15): the ports…' sits above agentsInUse (doctor.ts:223). The slot port formula is repeated in four places (core decide/receipts.ts:86, store worktree.ts:33, store leases.ts:156, cli runtime/worktrees.ts:44). GROUP_OF (cli commands/config.ts:18) restates MACHINE/PERSON/TEAM_KEYS. Moved-key knowledge lives in three places (MOVED, REMOVED_NOTE, legacyConfig). DEFAULT_CONFIG hard-codes claim 10m/3m20s instead of claimTiming(DEFAULT_INTERVAL). ResolvedConfig.agent is Type.String, not AgentName.
Axis: standards
